applyTo: '**'
description: "Use when generating, reviewing, running unit/component tests or checking coverage with Unit Test MCP."
---
# Unit Test MCP

Use these rules for unit/component tests only. End-to-end tools such as Playwright, Cypress and Selenium keep their existing workflows.

## Always use MCP tools
NEVER run test commands in a terminal, including chained npm/CI/validation scripts. Lint and compilation may use the normal repository tools; tests use MCP.
- Run or validate tests: call `run_tests` immediately. Fresh coverage means `include_coverage=true`, not reading old artifacts.
- Generate/improve one file: call `generate_test` BEFORE reading source/test files or authoring tests. Pass `source_file_path` and the existing `test_file_path` when known; it returns guidance, not finished tests.
- Folder work: call `generate_tests_batch` with `output_mode='structured'`, confirm large/ambiguous scope, then complete one file's full cycle at a time.
- Review existing/changed tests: call `review_test` with the source path and intended `test_type` when known. After generation, reuse its `resolvedTestType`. Do not substitute execution for this gate.
- Inspect existing coverage: call `inspect_coverage`. For a repair loop, use the same `source_file` and fresh returned `coverage_dir`/`run_id`, not a repository-wide dump.
- Find tests: use `find_test_files`; respect the repository's existing layout.
- Missing tools: STOP and ask to start Unit Test MCP/reload VS Code; never fall back to manual test execution.

## Protective workflow
Mandatory test workflow for generation/improvement:
1. Read the real source, existing tests, project configuration and shared test setup. Matching source/test repository instructions override generic framework defaults. Read any matching rules listed as omitted or truncated before authoring.
2. Do NOT modify source code without permission. Preserve existing assertions. Put the exact "Generated by AI (UnitTest MCP)" line-comment on line 1, using the test language's comment syntax.
3. Keep the behavior under test real. Mock external/platform/network/unsupported-browser boundaries and nondeterminism; owned collaborators may be isolated at justified unit-test boundaries. Preserve real composition within integration scope. Observing spies and actual-preserving factories are allowed. Reuse fixtures and honor repository isolation rules.
4. Assert independently specified meaningful contracts; prefer toStrictEqual for complete JS/TS objects you own. Partial value assertions are advisory: justify why omitted fields are outside the contract. Keep inputs correctly typed; no "as any"/"as unknown as" on asserted values or mock returns. Keep cases independent and deterministic.
5. Cover meaningful success, boundary, error, early-return and async transitions. Each test must fail when its named behavior breaks. Do not replace real behavior with constant snapshots or call-only smoke tests.
6. Fix lint/compile diagnostics, then call review_test with source/test paths and test_type set to generate_test's resolvedTestType. Resolve every block, address or justify warnings, and answer every semantic self-review item. Do not change test_type merely to silence findings. Never add protective-test suppression comments.
7. Run run_tests with include_coverage=true, an explicit test_pattern and scope='file' for one source, or scope='directory' with scope_path for a folder. Tests must pass and coverage.met must meet the tool-reported target; missing coverage is not success. Never run test commands in a terminal or use old coverage as validation.
8. If coverage is below target, use fresh coverage.fileDetails gaps when detailAvailable permits; otherwise call inspect_coverage for that same source with the returned coverage_dir/run_id. Read uncovered paths, add meaningful tests, review and rerun. Repeat at most five times, then report remaining gaps honestly rather than claiming completion.
9. For multiple files, finish generation, review, passing execution and scoped coverage for one file BEFORE beginning the next. Local protective review remains mandatory.

## Parameters and guidance
Choose the framework from the nearest project config: Jest/Vitest from package.json, pytest from Python configuration, .NET from its test project, or custom from the configured command. Preserve framework and project root across the cycle.
Use absolute `root_dir` paths on Windows. JS runners need a package.json with test configuration; Python needs its configured environment/project; .NET needs the solution/test project. Prefer explicit test file paths over keyword stems.
`generate_test` returns the complete framework guide, including worked examples, without a mode selection or filename-based guidance filter. Custom and matching repository instructions remain authoritative. Read any matching files identified as omitted/truncated. If the selected test path changes, refresh guidance with that explicit `test_file_path`.
AI attribution on line 1 is `// Generated by AI (UnitTest MCP)` for JS/TS/C#, `# Generated by AI (UnitTest MCP)` for Python, or the language's line-comment syntax with that exact text.

## `review_test` — protective-test gate
Resolve every block finding and answer its semantic checklist. New behavioral AST checks target JS/TS; the checklist also covers semantic and cross-language judgments. Do not add protective-test suppression comments.
First-party ownership alone is not a violation: judge mocks against the declared test boundary. Partial value assertions require contextual review, not automatic expansion to unrelated fields.
Coverage percentage alone is not quality: retain independently specified expectations, real first-party behavior, correctly typed data and deterministic outcomes. Preserve regression comments and bug context.
If three consecutive executions fail, re-read project configuration and retry once. If path/framework inference remains ambiguous, ask rather than guessing. Report missing data and remaining coverage gaps honestly.
